questions.q: In a workspace enabled for Unity Catalog, what does navigational search review when you search for a table by text string?
options: Table names, table comments, column names, and column comments
Only the exact table name
Only the catalog and schema names
Only columns marked with a PII tag
questions.explain: Unity Catalog search looks at table names, table comments, column names, and column comments, so a well-described table is findable even with an obscure name.

questions.q: What is a 'knowledge card' in Azure Databricks search results?
options: Inline metadata shown for a high-confidence top search result, generated from the object's AI comments
A printable PDF summary of a table's full schema
A card game used to onboard new Databricks admins
A required approval step before a table can be queried
questions.explain: When search identifies a match with high confidence, the top result becomes a knowledge card showing extra object metadata inline instead of just a link.

questions.q: What search syntax finds every object tagged with a governed or ordinary tag key 'lodging'?
options: tag:lodging
class:lodging
SELECT TAG lodging
FILTER(lodging)
questions.explain: The tag:<tag_key> syntax (or tag:<tag_key>:<tag_value> to match a specific value) searches for objects carrying that tag.

questions.q: Which SQL command lists all tables in a given schema, for programmatic discovery without the UI?
options: SHOW TABLES IN <schema>
LIST TABLES FROM <schema>
GET TABLES <schema>
DISCOVER TABLES <schema>
questions.explain: SHOW TABLES IN <catalog>.<schema> lists the tables in that schema, the same command a pipeline or CI job would use for discovery.

questions.q: Can a user's search return a table they do not have SELECT or BROWSE permission on?
options: No — search only returns objects the querying user has permission to see
Yes, but only the table name, not its contents
Yes, if the table has a governed tag
Yes, if the search uses semantic (natural-language) search instead of keyword search
questions.explain: Search respects Unity Catalog's privilege model exactly — a table the user lacks permission on simply never appears in results, regardless of search method.
